summary: This note is an encyclopedia-style overview of Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia, covering its former names, location on Java, and role as the country's economic, cultural and political center. It gives population figures for the city and for the Greater Jakarta metropolitan area known as Jabodetabek. It also explains that Jakarta is officially a province with special capital region status but is commonly called a city.
one_line: Overview of Jakarta, Indonesia's capital on northwest Java, its former names, population, and the Jabodetabek metropolitan area.
key_facts: Jakarta is the capital of Indonesia and is officially named the Special Capital Region of Jakarta.
Jakarta was formerly known as Batavia during the Dutch East Indies period.
Jakarta was known as Sunda Kelapa during the Sunda Kingdom.
Jakarta is located on the northwest coast of Java, described as the world's most populous island.
Jakarta is the center of economics, culture and politics of Indonesia.
Jakarta had a population of 10,075,310 as of 2014.
The Greater Jakarta metropolitan area is known as Jabodetabek.
The name Jabodetabek is formed by combining the initial syllables of Jakarta, Bogor, Depok, Tangerang and Bekasi.
Jabodetabek is described as the second largest urban agglomeration and 2nd largest city area in the world after Tokyo.
Jabodetabek had a population of 30,214,303 inhabitants as of the 2010 census.
Jakarta's business opportunities and potential for a higher standard of living attract migrants from all over the Indonesian archipelago.
Jakarta is a melting pot of many communities and cultures because of migration.
Jakarta is officially a province with special capital region status, yet is commonly referred to as a city.
The Jakarta provincial government administers five administrative cities and one administrative regency.
